stem:
A 32-year-old primigravida at 34 plus 3 weeks gestation is admitted from clinic with a headache and epigastric pain. Her blood pressure recorded three times over 30 minutes is 168/112, 172/108 and 170/110. She has 3+ proteinuria on dipstick and a spot protein to creatinine ratio of 65 mg/mmol (less than 30). She has brisk lower limb reflexes with 4 beats of clonus on the right.

On examination she is uncomfortable but alert. Uterine tone is soft, cardiotocography is normal with a reactive trace, and there are no vaginal loss or contractions. Full blood count shows a platelet count of 135 x10 to the 9 per litre (150-400), alanine aminotransferase 90 U/L (less than 35), creatinine 82 micromol/L (45-90) and lactate dehydrogenase 340 U/L (less than 250). Antenatal corticosteroids for lung maturation were given three days ago in another episode of admission.

data_table.Vital signs: pulse rate 96, blood pressure 170/110, respiratory rate 18, SpO2 99 percent on room air, temperature 36.8 degrees, fetal heart rate 145
data_table.Investigations: haemoglobin 118 g/L (115-165), platelets 135 x10 to the 9 per litre (150-400), ALT 90 U/L (less than 35), creatinine 82 micromol/L (45-90), LDH 340 U/L (less than 250), urate 0.42 mmol/L (0.15-0.36)

lead_in: In addition to intravenous antihypertensive therapy, what is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Administer intravenous phenytoin 15 mg/kg loading dose as an alternative to magnesium sulfate seizure prophylaxis
options.rationale: Magnesium sulfate is superior to phenytoin for both prevention and treatment of eclamptic seizures (MAGPIE and Collaborative Eclampsia trials). Phenytoin is not first-line. (Source: SOMANZ Hypertension in Pregnancy Guideline)

options.text: Administer intramuscular betamethasone 11.4 mg as a repeat antenatal corticosteroid dose for lung maturation
options.rationale: Corticosteroids were given three days ago and repeat dosing is not indicated so soon; more importantly, the priority now is seizure prophylaxis and delivery planning, not lung maturation. (Source: SOMANZ Hypertension in Pregnancy Guideline)

options.text: Administer intravenous furosemide 40 mg as diuretic therapy for suspected preeclampsia-related pulmonary oedema
options.rationale: There are no clinical or oxygenation findings to suggest pulmonary oedema and diuresis is not part of seizure prophylaxis. (Source: SOMANZ Hypertension in Pregnancy Guideline)

options.text: Commence intravenous magnesium sulfate 4 g loading dose over 20 minutes then 1 g/hour maintenance infusion
options.rationale: Severe preeclampsia with neurological features (headache, hyperreflexia, clonus) meets SOMANZ criteria for magnesium sulfate seizure prophylaxis. The 4 g load followed by 1 g/hour infusion is the AU standard. (Source: SOMANZ Hypertension in Pregnancy Guideline)

options.text: Administer intravenous diazepam 10 mg as a prophylactic anticonvulsant while transfer to a tertiary unit is arranged
options.rationale: Benzodiazepines are used for seizures resistant to magnesium sulfate but not as first-line prophylaxis in preeclampsia. (Source: SOMANZ Hypertension in Pregnancy Guideline)

explanation.summary: Severe preeclampsia with neurological signs (headache, hyperreflexia, clonus) and biochemical involvement (raised ALT, thrombocytopenia, raised urate) is a SOMANZ indication for magnesium sulfate seizure prophylaxis. The AU regimen is a 4 g load over 20 minutes and a 1 g/hour maintenance infusion. Antihypertensive therapy and planning for delivery run in parallel.
key_points: MgSO4 4 g IV load over 20 min then 1 g/hour infusion; monitor knee reflexes, respiratory rate, and urine output
MgSO4 is superior to phenytoin and diazepam for both prevention and treatment of eclamptic seizures
Severe preeclampsia = severe hypertension plus organ involvement OR neurological features
explanation.pearls: Loss of patellar reflexes is the first sign of magnesium toxicity. Calcium gluconate 1 g IV is the antidote.

subtopic_detail: Anti-D immunoglobulin timing after sensitising event
stem:
A 24-year-old primigravida at 22 weeks gestation presents 6 hours after a minor motor vehicle crash. She was a restrained front seat passenger in a low-speed rear-ending collision, has no abdominal pain, no per vaginal bleeding, no uterine tenderness on palpation and a reassuring cardiotocography trace. Fetal biometry is appropriate for gestation on point-of-care ultrasound with an anterior placenta well clear of the internal os.

Her booking blood group is O rhesus negative with no red cell antibodies detected at 28 week screen (which has not yet been performed at her current gestation). She has previously declined the 28-week prophylactic anti-D dose plan but consents today to being managed as clinically indicated. She is otherwise well and has no other injuries.

data_table.Vital signs: within normal limits
data_table.Investigations: haemoglobin 122 g/L (115-165), blood group O rhesus negative, indirect antiglobulin test negative, Kleihauer-Betke test pending

lead_in: What is the most appropriate next step regarding anti-D immunoglobulin?

options.text: Await the Kleihauer-Betke test result before deciding whether to administer any anti-D immunoglobulin at all
options.rationale: Anti-D should not be delayed for the Kleihauer-Betke. The initial 625 IU dose is given first; Kleihauer only guides ADDITIONAL doses beyond that. (Source: NBA Guidelines for the use of Rh(D) Immunoglobulin)
source_refs: NBA Guidelines for the use of Rh(D) Immunoglobulin

options.text: Administer intramuscular anti-D immunoglobulin 250 IU now given the minor severity of the mechanism of injury
options.rationale: The 250 IU dose is used before 12 weeks; from 12 weeks onward the AU standard dose is 625 IU regardless of the severity of the sensitising event. (Source: NBA Guidelines for the use of Rh(D) Immunoglobulin)
source_refs: NBA Guidelines for the use of Rh(D) Immunoglobulin

options.text: Withhold anti-D immunoglobulin because the placenta is anterior and the motor vehicle mechanism is very low grade
options.rationale: Placental location and mechanism grade do not exclude sensitisation risk. Any abdominal trauma after 12 weeks in a rhesus D negative woman is a potentially sensitising event. (Source: NBA Guidelines for the use of Rh(D) Immunoglobulin)
source_refs: NBA Guidelines for the use of Rh(D) Immunoglobulin

options.text: Administer intramuscular anti-D immunoglobulin 1500 IU now as a routine 28 week prophylactic dose in advance
options.rationale: The 1500 IU is the routine 28-week prophylactic dose, not the event-triggered dose. Event doses are 625 IU (from 12 weeks) or 250 IU (under 12 weeks). (Source: NBA Guidelines for the use of Rh(D) Immunoglobulin)
source_refs: NBA Guidelines for the use of Rh(D) Immunoglobulin

options.text: Administer intramuscular anti-D immunoglobulin 625 IU now and await Kleihauer-Betke to guide any additional dose
options.rationale: For a potentially sensitising event after 12 weeks in a rhesus D negative woman, NBA recommends 625 IU IM anti-D within 72 hours (ideally as soon as possible). The Kleihauer-Betke test then quantifies fetomaternal haemorrhage to guide additional dosing if required. (Source: NBA Guidelines for the use of Rh(D) Immunoglobulin)
source_refs: NBA Guidelines for the use of Rh(D) Immunoglobulin

explanation.summary: This woman has had a potentially sensitising event after 12 weeks. NBA guidance is to give 625 IU IM anti-D as soon as possible (and within 72 hours). Kleihauer-Betke testing quantifies fetomaternal haemorrhage and guides any additional doses. The 1500 IU prophylactic 28-week dose is a separate schedule.
key_points: Event doses: 250 IU under 12 weeks; 625 IU from 12 weeks onward; Kleihauer guides additional dosing
Routine 28 and 34 week prophylactic doses are 625 IU each (or a single 1500 IU dose depending on local schedule)
Do not wait for Kleihauer to give the first event dose
explanation.pearls: Every 4 mL of fetal red cells requires an additional 625 IU. Read the Kleihauer as a dose driver, not a gate.

sources.label: NBA Guidelines for the use of Rh(D) Immunoglobulin
RANZCOG C-Obs 6 Guidelines for the use of Rh(D) Immunoglobulin

stem:
A 32-year-old woman with a body mass index of 26 attends a diabetes in pregnancy clinic at 27 weeks gestation after a 75 g oral glucose tolerance test performed at 26 weeks in her local pathology lab. Her fasting glucose was 5.1 mmol/L, 1-hour glucose 9.8 mmol/L, and 2-hour glucose 8.3 mmol/L (fasting less than 5.1, 1-hour less than 10.0, 2-hour less than 8.5). She has no personal history of type 2 diabetes, no polycystic ovary syndrome, and her first pregnancy 3 years ago was uncomplicated with a birth weight of 3300 g.

Her first-trimester screening glucose was normal. Booking bloods showed normal HbA1c at 5.3 percent (under 5.7). She is asymptomatic with no polyuria or polydipsia. Fetal biometry at 27 weeks shows appropriate growth with abdominal circumference on the 60th centile.

data_table.Vital signs: within normal limits
data_table.Investigations: OGTT fasting 5.1 mmol/L (less than 5.1), 1-hour 9.8 mmol/L (less than 10.0), 2-hour 8.3 mmol/L (less than 8.5), HbA1c 5.3 percent (less than 5.7)

lead_in: What is the most appropriate diagnostic interpretation and next step?

options.text: Diagnose gestational diabetes based on the fasting value meeting the threshold and commence structured dietary advice and self blood glucose monitoring
options.rationale: ADIPS applies IADPSG cut-offs where meeting or exceeding any one of fasting 5.1, 1-hour 10.0, or 2-hour 8.5 mmol/L confirms GDM. Her fasting value of 5.1 meets the fasting threshold, so GDM is diagnosed on this single value. (Source: ADIPS Consensus Guidelines for the Diagnosis of Gestational Diabetes)
source_refs: ADIPS Consensus Guidelines for the Diagnosis of Gestational Diabetes

options.text: Repeat the oral glucose tolerance test in 4 weeks because none of the individual values definitively exceeded the diagnostic thresholds today
options.rationale: The fasting value of 5.1 meets the threshold (the criterion is greater than or equal to, not strictly greater than). GDM should be diagnosed and treated now. (Source: ADIPS Consensus Guidelines for the Diagnosis of Gestational Diabetes)
source_refs: ADIPS Consensus Guidelines for the Diagnosis of Gestational Diabetes

options.text: Reassure that gestational diabetes is excluded because at least two values are required to meet the diagnostic thresholds under the ADIPS pathway
options.rationale: ADIPS requires only one abnormal value on the 75 g OGTT to diagnose GDM. (Source: ADIPS Consensus Guidelines for the Diagnosis of Gestational Diabetes)
source_refs: ADIPS Consensus Guidelines for the Diagnosis of Gestational Diabetes

options.text: Diagnose overt diabetes in pregnancy based on the OGTT results and commence subcutaneous insulin as first-line pharmacotherapy today
options.rationale: Overt diabetes in pregnancy requires fasting glucose at or above 7.0, HbA1c at or above 6.5 percent, or random glucose at or above 11.1. Her values are consistent with GDM, not overt diabetes. (Source: ADIPS Consensus Guidelines for the Diagnosis of Gestational Diabetes)
source_refs: ADIPS Consensus Guidelines for the Diagnosis of Gestational Diabetes

options.text: Repeat the HbA1c and treat as gestational diabetes only if the result rises to at least 6.5 percent on the follow-up sample
options.rationale: HbA1c is not used to diagnose or exclude GDM; the OGTT is the diagnostic test. HbA1c at or above 6.5 percent flags overt diabetes, not GDM. (Source: ADIPS Consensus Guidelines for the Diagnosis of Gestational Diabetes)
source_refs: ADIPS Consensus Guidelines for the Diagnosis of Gestational Diabetes

explanation.summary: The ADIPS diagnostic thresholds for GDM on a 75 g OGTT are fasting at or above 5.1 mmol/L, 1-hour at or above 10.0, and 2-hour at or above 8.5. Any one value meeting or exceeding its threshold confirms the diagnosis. Her fasting value of exactly 5.1 mmol/L therefore meets criteria. Dietary advice and self blood glucose monitoring are first-line.
key_points: ADIPS/IADPSG OGTT thresholds: fasting 5.1, 1-hour 10.0, 2-hour 8.5 mmol/L (any one confirms GDM)
Overt diabetes in pregnancy: fasting at or above 7.0, HbA1c at or above 6.5 percent, random at or above 11.1
First-line management is diet and self-monitoring; escalate to metformin then insulin as needed
explanation.pearls: The cut-off is greater-than-or-equal, not strictly greater: a fasting value exactly on the cut-off IS diagnostic in Australia.

sources.label: ADIPS Consensus Guidelines for the Diagnosis of Gestational Diabetes
RANZCOG C-Obs 7 Diagnosis of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus

subtopic_detail: Postpartum haemorrhage escalation beyond first-line uterotonics
stem:
A 33-year-old multiparous woman has just delivered a live infant weighing 4200 g vaginally after a 60 minute second stage and active management of the third stage with intramuscular oxytocin 10 units. Estimated blood loss at 10 minutes postpartum is 1200 mL from ongoing dark red bleeding per vagina with a boggy fundus at the level of the umbilicus.

Examination under good lighting demonstrates an intact perineum and second-degree perineal tear that has been repaired without ongoing bleeding from the wound. The lower uterine segment is empty on bimanual examination and the placenta was inspected and reported as complete. Bimanual uterine compression and a further intravenous oxytocin 10 unit slow bolus with intramuscular ergometrine 250 microgram have been given but the fundus remains soft and bleeding continues at 200 mL per 5 minutes. Blood pressure is 92/58 with pulse rate 122. There is no history of hypertension, coronary disease, or asthma.

data_table.Vital signs: pulse rate 122, blood pressure 92/58, respiratory rate 22, SpO2 99 percent on room air, temperature 36.8 degrees
data_table.Investigations: haemoglobin 92 g/L (115-165) on point-of-care testing, thromboelastography pending, blood group known O rhesus positive with active group and hold

lead_in: What is the most appropriate next uterotonic step?

options.text: Administer repeat intramuscular ergometrine 250 microgram as the second dose within 5 minutes of the first dose given
options.rationale: Ergometrine dose is capped and repeat doses within a short interval risk severe hypertension and coronary spasm. Escalation to a different agent (carboprost or misoprostol) is required. (Source: RANZCOG C-Obs 43 Prevention, Detection and Management of PPH)
source_refs: RANZCOG C-Obs 43 Prevention, Detection and Management of PPH

options.text: Administer intramuscular carboprost 250 microgram (repeated every 15 minutes to a maximum of 8 doses) with continuing bimanual compression
options.rationale: For atonic postpartum haemorrhage refractory to oxytocin and ergometrine, the next uterotonic in the RANZCOG PPH cascade is carboprost 250 microgram IM (or into the myometrium), repeated as needed. She has no asthma contraindication. (Source: RANZCOG C-Obs 43 Prevention, Detection and Management of PPH)
source_refs: RANZCOG C-Obs 43 Prevention, Detection and Management of PPH

options.text: Commence intravenous magnesium sulfate 4 g loading bolus over 20 minutes for suspected retained postpartum uterine relaxation
options.rationale: Magnesium relaxes uterine muscle and would worsen atony. It has no role in PPH management. (Source: RANZCOG C-Obs 43 Prevention, Detection and Management of PPH)
source_refs: RANZCOG C-Obs 43 Prevention, Detection and Management of PPH

options.text: Administer intramuscular oxytocin 10 units as a third dose to overcome the persistent atony via peripheral receptor upregulation
options.rationale: Oxytocin receptors desensitise with repeated dosing during postpartum haemorrhage. A different pharmacological class is required at this stage of the cascade. (Source: RANZCOG C-Obs 43 Prevention, Detection and Management of PPH)
source_refs: RANZCOG C-Obs 43 Prevention, Detection and Management of PPH

options.text: Administer intravenous tranexamic acid 1 g slow bolus alone and continue observation of uterine tone without further uterotonics
options.rationale: Tranexamic acid 1 g IV is indicated (WOMAN trial) and should be given, but it does not replace ongoing uterotonic escalation for a still-atonic uterus. (Source: RANZCOG C-Obs 43 Prevention, Detection and Management of PPH)
source_refs: RANZCOG C-Obs 43 Prevention, Detection and Management of PPH

explanation.summary: This is atonic PPH refractory to first-line oxytocin and ergometrine. The next uterotonic in the RANZCOG cascade is carboprost 250 microgram IM every 15 minutes (max 8 doses) provided the woman is not asthmatic. Tranexamic acid 1 g IV should be given in parallel per the WOMAN trial and blood products activated. Mechanical measures (bimanual compression, intrauterine balloon) continue throughout.
key_points: PPH uterotonic ladder: oxytocin, ergometrine (contra in HTN/CAD), carboprost (contra in asthma), misoprostol PR
TXA 1 g IV within 3 hours halves death from bleeding (WOMAN trial)
Repeat oxytocin has diminishing return due to receptor desensitisation
explanation.pearls: Ergometrine's contraindication is hypertension and coronary disease; carboprost's is asthma. Read the case for the contraindication that decides between them.

sources.label: RANZCOG C-Obs 43 Prevention, Detection and Management of PPH
WOMAN Trial Collaborators. Effect of early tranexamic acid administration on mortality in women with PPH. Lancet 2017

subtopic_detail: Recurrent APH from placenta praevia at 32 weeks
stem:
A 34-year-old woman gravida 3 para 2 with two prior lower segment caesarean sections presents at 32 weeks gestation with her second episode of painless vaginal bleeding this admission. The previous episode was 5 days ago and settled after 200 mL of loss with a course of intramuscular betamethasone commenced at that time (second dose given 24 hours ago). She has been inpatient since.

Today she has passed approximately 400 mL of fresh red blood over 30 minutes with a soft, non-tender uterus. Fetal biometry a week ago showed appropriate growth. A repeat cardiotocograph is reactive with baseline 145 with normal variability and no decelerations. Her booking transvaginal ultrasound confirmed a complete placenta praevia with a posterior placenta covering the internal os; there was no ultrasound evidence of a morbidly adherent placenta but this was not formally excluded on MRI.

data_table.Vital signs: pulse rate 104, blood pressure 108/68, respiratory rate 20, SpO2 99 percent on room air, temperature 36.8 degrees, fetal heart rate 145
data_table.Investigations: haemoglobin 96 g/L (115-165) (was 110 g/L one week ago), platelets 220 x10 to the 9 per litre (150-400), coagulation studies within normal limits, blood group A rhesus positive with two units crossmatched and available

lead_in: What is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.text: Attempt vaginal delivery after amniotomy and syntocinon augmentation once corticosteroids are complete and bleeding settles again
options.rationale: Complete placenta praevia is an absolute contraindication to vaginal delivery. Attempting labour risks massive haemorrhage. (Source: RANZCOG C-Obs 20 Placenta Praevia and Placenta Accreta)
source_refs: RANZCOG C-Obs 20 Placenta Praevia and Placenta Accreta

options.text: Insert an intrauterine balloon tamponade device to control bleeding and continue expectant management to at least 37 weeks
options.rationale: Intrauterine balloon tamponade is a postpartum tool for uterine atony and is not used antenatally in placenta praevia. (Source: RANZCOG C-Obs 20 Placenta Praevia and Placenta Accreta)
source_refs: RANZCOG C-Obs 20 Placenta Praevia and Placenta Accreta

options.text: Arrange delivery by elective caesarean section under general anaesthesia within the next 24 hours after multidisciplinary team review
options.rationale: A second sentinel bleed of at least 400 mL in a woman with placenta praevia and prior caesarean scars at 32 weeks after completed antenatal corticosteroids is an accepted RANZCOG indication for expedited caesarean delivery. Multidisciplinary planning (obstetrics, anaesthesia, neonatology, blood bank, interventional radiology) is essential given the risk of placenta accreta spectrum. (Source: RANZCOG C-Obs 20 Placenta Praevia and Placenta Accreta)
source_refs: RANZCOG C-Obs 20 Placenta Praevia and Placenta Accreta

options.text: Commence intravenous magnesium sulfate as neuroprotection and continue expectant management targeting delivery at 34 weeks gestation
options.rationale: Magnesium sulfate for neuroprotection is used with imminent preterm birth under 30 weeks, not at 32 weeks. It does not address ongoing haemorrhage. (Source: RANZCOG C-Obs 20 Placenta Praevia and Placenta Accreta)
source_refs: RANZCOG C-Obs 20 Placenta Praevia and Placenta Accreta

options.text: Administer intravenous tranexamic acid 1 g and repeat the transvaginal ultrasound to reconfirm the placental location today
options.rationale: Antenatal transvaginal ultrasound has already confirmed complete praevia. Repeat imaging does not change management in the setting of recurrent significant bleeding. (Source: RANZCOG C-Obs 20 Placenta Praevia and Placenta Accreta)
source_refs: RANZCOG C-Obs 20 Placenta Praevia and Placenta Accreta

explanation.summary: A second sentinel bleed in a woman with placenta praevia and two prior caesarean sections at 32 weeks is a strong indication for delivery. Corticosteroids for lung maturation are complete, blood is available, and multidisciplinary planning must be activated given the risk of placenta accreta spectrum given the caesarean history. Continued expectancy risks catastrophic haemorrhage.
key_points: Complete praevia contraindicates vaginal delivery absolutely
Prior caesarean scars plus anterior praevia raise accreta risk; MDT planning and interventional radiology backup are standard
Recurrent APH at or after 32 weeks with completed corticosteroids justifies expedited delivery
explanation.pearls: The threshold to deliver in praevia is set by the bleed pattern, not the calendar. A sentinel bleed at 32 weeks post-steroids trumps the elective 36 to 37 week schedule.

sources.label: RANZCOG C-Obs 20 Placenta Praevia and Placenta Accreta

subtopic_detail: Historical bilaterality flip in ectopic surgical choice
stem:
A 34-year-old woman gravida 3 para 1 presents to a regional emergency department with 4 hours of severe right iliac fossa pain, dizziness and one episode of syncope. On arrival she is pale, cool peripherally with a heart rate of 128 and blood pressure of 88/50. She has abdominal guarding maximal in the right iliac fossa, and cervical excitation on gentle speculum examination. Point-of-care ultrasound in ED shows a moderate volume of free fluid in the pouch of Douglas and no intrauterine pregnancy.

Her past history includes a laparoscopic LEFT salpingectomy 3 years ago for a ruptured left tubal ectopic and a subsequent spontaneous term vaginal delivery 18 months ago. Her right fallopian tube was visualised as intact at the previous operation. She has had no fertility treatment. Serum beta hCG on arrival is 6800 IU/L. Two units of crossmatched blood are available and initial resuscitation has been commenced. She and her partner have consented in principle to whatever surgery is needed to save life.

data_table.Vital signs: pulse rate 128, blood pressure 88/50, respiratory rate 24, SpO2 99 percent on room air, temperature 36.8 degrees
data_table.Investigations: beta hCG 6800 IU/L, haemoglobin 88 g/L (115-165) (was 128 g/L one month ago), platelets 220 x10 to the 9 per litre (150-400), blood group A rhesus positive
data_table.Operative findings: at laparoscopy: 500 mL of intraperitoneal blood, ruptured right ampullary ectopic with active bleeding, left fallopian tube absent (prior salpingectomy), otherwise normal uterus and right ovary

lead_in: What is the most appropriate operative procedure?

options.text: Proceed with right salpingostomy to preserve the only remaining tube for the possibility of future natural conception attempts
options.rationale: The textbook default of salpingostomy when it is the last tube is inverted in this scenario: the woman has already had a subsequent spontaneous term pregnancy (proving contralateral tubal absence is not preventing conception) and salpingostomy in the only tube risks persistent trophoblast requiring methotrexate or repeat surgery, plus recurrent ectopic in the same damaged tube. Definitive salpingectomy plus IVF planning is the safer long-term choice. (Source: RANZCOG C-Obs 61 Ectopic Pregnancy)

options.text: Perform emergency laparotomy with total abdominal hysterectomy for definitive haemorrhage control in the shocked patient
options.rationale: Hysterectomy is not required for a ruptured tubal ectopic and is not the appropriate procedure. Salpingectomy alone controls bleeding. (Source: RANZCOG C-Obs 61 Ectopic Pregnancy)

options.text: Administer intramuscular methotrexate 50 mg/m2 and close the abdomen without proceeding to definitive resection today
options.rationale: Methotrexate is contraindicated in a ruptured, actively bleeding ectopic with haemodynamic instability. Surgery is mandatory. (Source: RANZCOG C-Obs 61 Ectopic Pregnancy)

options.text: Proceed with right salpingectomy to control haemorrhage and prevent same-tube recurrence in the only remaining tube
options.rationale: Meta-analysis (ESEP trial, Mol 2014) shows salpingostomy and salpingectomy have similar future intrauterine pregnancy rates when the contralateral tube is present, but salpingostomy carries a 4 to 8 percent persistent trophoblast rate and higher recurrence in the same tube. Where the contralateral tube is ABSENT, recurrence in the affected tube becomes a dominant future risk and RANZCOG accepts salpingectomy to definitively remove that risk despite the loss of natural conception potential; IVF preserves fertility options. (Source: RANZCOG C-Obs 61 Ectopic Pregnancy)

options.text: Perform right salpingotomy with placement of a subtubal ligation to prevent same tube recurrence in future cycles
options.rationale: Subtubal ligation without resection does not control acute bleeding and creates a functionally non-viable tube while leaving trophoblastic tissue in situ. It is not a recognised operation for ruptured tubal ectopic. (Source: RANZCOG C-Obs 61 Ectopic Pregnancy)

explanation.summary: The routine teaching that salpingostomy is preferred when the contralateral tube is absent is inverted here by the specific history. This woman has already achieved a subsequent term pregnancy and the risk of recurrent ectopic in the affected tube plus persistent trophoblast after salpingostomy outweigh the benefit of tubal preservation. Right salpingectomy is definitive and IVF preserves future fertility options.
key_points: Salpingostomy versus salpingectomy: similar future pregnancy rates when contralateral tube present (ESEP trial)
Absent contralateral tube shifts the calculus toward salpingectomy when the woman has proven fertility or accepts IVF
Ruptured ectopic with haemodynamic instability mandates surgery, not methotrexate
explanation.pearls: Historical bilaterality (prior contralateral salpingectomy, mastectomy, nephrectomy) is a classical trickiness lever. The tube you preserve may be more of a liability than an asset if it is the tube that has already failed.

sources.label: Mol F et al. Salpingotomy versus salpingectomy in women with tubal pregnancy (ESEP). Lancet 2014

stem:
A 32-year-old G2P1 has just delivered a 3900 g baby vaginally after a spontaneous labour and second stage of 40 minutes. Twenty minutes after birth she has ongoing bright red vaginal bleeding estimated at 1000 mL with clot expression. Her uterus feels soft and bulky above the umbilicus.

She has already received 10 units of intramuscular oxytocin as third-stage prophylaxis and the placenta was delivered complete. Her booking blood pressure was 118/72 mmHg. She had no antenatal hypertension and has taken no cardiovascular medications.

data_table.Vital signs: Pulse 118/min, blood pressure 96/62 mmHg, respiratory rate 22/min, SpO2 99 percent on room air, temperature 36.9 degrees C
data_table.Examination: Boggy uterus above umbilicus, actively bleeding; placenta delivered complete; no cervical or vaginal tears identified on inspection
data_table.Investigations: Group and hold sent, cross-match ordered; venous access with two 16G cannulae; oxytocin infusion prepared

lead_in: What is the most appropriate next pharmacological step?

options.text: Intramuscular ergometrine 250 micrograms with intravenous tranexamic acid 1 g
options.rationale: Ergometrine is the second-line uterotonic (after oxytocin) for atonic PPH in a normotensive woman, and TXA within 3 hours reduces PPH mortality. (Source: RANZCOG PPH statement; WOMAN trial)

options.text: Intramuscular carboprost 250 micrograms into the deltoid with continued oxytocin
options.rationale: Carboprost is third-line after failure of oxytocin plus ergometrine and is administered intramuscular into a large muscle mass at 250 micrograms up to eight doses. (Source: RANZCOG: Management of postpartum haemorrhage)

options.text: Intravenous ergometrine 500 micrograms slow push with continuous oxytocin infusion
options.rationale: IV ergometrine is second choice route (IM preferred), 500 micrograms is above standard dose, and giving without TXA misses the mortality benefit. (Source: RANZCOG: Management of postpartum haemorrhage)

options.text: Sublingual misoprostol 800 micrograms and observe for uterine tone response
options.rationale: Misoprostol is a fourth-line uterotonic when oxytocin, ergometrine and carboprost fail or are contraindicated; not appropriate before trying second-line. (Source: RANZCOG: Management of postpartum haemorrhage)

options.text: Intramuscular oxytocin 10 units second dose with continuous oxytocin infusion 40 units
options.rationale: Repeat oxytocin bolus adds little once the receptor is saturated; escalation to ergometrine plus TXA is standard second-line. (Source: RANZCOG: Management of postpartum haemorrhage)

explanation.summary: The RANZCOG PPH algorithm escalates uterotonics through oxytocin, then ergometrine, then carboprost, then misoprostol, with tranexamic acid 1 g IV added early once PPH is diagnosed. The WOMAN trial established a mortality benefit for TXA within three hours of PPH onset. Ergometrine is contraindicated in hypertension and pre-eclampsia; carboprost is contraindicated in asthma. Concurrent mechanical measures (bimanual compression, catheterisation) run alongside pharmacology.
key_points: Uterotonic sequence: oxytocin then ergometrine then carboprost then misoprostol.
TXA 1 g IV within 3 hours of PPH onset (WOMAN trial).
Ergometrine contraindicated in hypertension.
Carboprost contraindicated in asthma.
explanation.pearls: Give ergometrine 250 mcg IM plus tranexamic acid 1 g IV as second-line for atonic PPH in a normotensive woman; TXA within 3 hours halves PPH mortality.

stem:
A 28-year-old G2P1 presents to the early pregnancy unit at 6 weeks by LMP with right iliac fossa discomfort and vaginal spotting. She is haemodynamically stable and pain is mild. Serum beta hCG is 4200 IU/L.

Transvaginal ultrasound shows an empty uterine cavity and a 2.6 cm right adnexal mass separate from the ovary with a yolk sac visible but no fetal pole and no cardiac activity. She has stopped breastfeeding her first child three months ago and is keen to avoid surgery if possible.

data_table.Vital signs: Pulse 84/min, blood pressure 118/72 mmHg, respiratory rate 16/min, SpO2 99 percent on room air, temperature 36.8 degrees C
data_table.Examination: Alert, comfortable at rest; mild right iliac fossa tenderness on palpation without guarding or rebound; no cervical excitation
data_table.Investigations: Beta hCG 4200 IU/L, haemoglobin 128 g/L (115 to 165), liver and renal function within normal limits, no free fluid on ultrasound

lead_in: What is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Expectant management with serial beta hCG measurement every 48 to 72 hours
options.rationale: Expectant management is reserved for asymptomatic women with hCG under 1500 IU/L and falling trends; this hCG is far too high. (Source: RANZCOG: Ectopic pregnancy)
source_refs: RANZCOG: Diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy

options.text: Laparoscopic salpingectomy of the affected tube under the acute gynaecology list
options.rationale: Salpingectomy is not first-choice when the patient is stable, meets methotrexate criteria and has fertility preservation goals with a healthy contralateral tube. (Source: RANZCOG: Ectopic pregnancy)
source_refs: RANZCOG: Diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy

options.text: Laparoscopic salpingostomy with preservation of the affected tube and cornual repair
options.rationale: Salpingostomy carries higher persistent trophoblast risk and is preferred only when the contralateral tube is absent or diseased. (Source: RANZCOG: Ectopic pregnancy)
source_refs: RANZCOG: Diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy

options.text: Intramuscular methotrexate 50 mg/m2 single dose with day 4 and day 7 hCG follow-up
options.rationale: This ectopic meets RANZCOG criteria for methotrexate: hCG under 5000, no cardiac activity, mass under 3.5 cm, minimal pain, stable, normal LFTs, reliable follow-up. (Source: RANZCOG: Ectopic pregnancy)
source_refs: RANZCOG: Diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy

options.text: Mifepristone 200 mg orally followed by misoprostol 800 micrograms vaginally at 48 hours
options.rationale: Mifepristone plus misoprostol is a medical abortion regimen for intrauterine pregnancy, not for ectopic pregnancy. (Source: RANZCOG: Ectopic pregnancy)
source_refs: RANZCOG: Diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy

explanation.summary: RANZCOG methotrexate criteria for ectopic pregnancy are: haemodynamic stability, no fetal cardiac activity, adnexal mass under 3.5 cm, serum hCG under 5000 IU/L, minimal pain, no significant haemoperitoneum, reliable follow-up and no methotrexate contraindications. Surgical management (salpingectomy preferred, salpingostomy if contralateral tube absent or diseased) is required when hCG is 5000 or above, cardiac activity is present, mass is 3.5 cm or larger, significant pain or haemodynamic compromise. Follow-up hCG on days 4 and 7 aims for at least a 15 percent drop between those two days; failing this triggers a second dose or surgery.
key_points: MTX threshold: hCG under 5000, no cardiac activity, mass under 3.5 cm.
MTX regimen: 50 mg/m2 IM single dose, day 4 and day 7 hCG.
Salpingectomy preferred over salpingostomy when contralateral tube healthy.
Mifepristone plus misoprostol is medical abortion, not ectopic treatment.
explanation.pearls: RANZCOG surgical threshold for tubal ectopic is hCG 5000 IU/L or above; below 5000 with all other MTX criteria met, single-dose IM methotrexate is preferred.
